newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch optimistic on compromise on dietary foodstuffs.
newsitem.headline: Dutch optimistic on compromise on dietary foodstuffs.

text.p: The Dutch presidency is optimistic that EU internal trade ministers will finally adopt on Thursday a compromise proposal on a common position concerning the harmonisation of national legislation on dietary foodstuffs.
A Dutch official said ahead of Thursday's meeting it looked quite promising.
Last year, the Internal Market Council failed to reach agreement on the proposal with the 14 other member states unable to agree to a German demand for an EU system for food for diabetics.
The Commission's proposal would modify directive 89/398/EEC which set up EU rules for the labelling, presentation and advertising of dietary foodstuffs.
The directive was part of the 1985 White Paper programme for the realisation of the single market.
The annex of this directive lists groups of foods for "particular nutritional uses for which specific provisions will be laid down by specific directives.". These would be adopted by the Commission.

The Commission had originally proposed to limit the categories of products requiring specific provisions to four instead of nine. These included cereal based foods and baby foods, food intended for weight control diets and dietary foods for special medical purposes.
Following the opinion of the European Parliament, the Commission added foods for persons suffering from diabetic disorders.
But member states had different views on the categories of special foodstuffs that required specific provisions.
Under the Dutch compromise, foods "adapted to intensive muscular activity, especially for sportsmen," would also be included in the annex.
Regarding foodstuffs for diabetics, a decision on the desirability of special provisions would be taken only after a transitional period.
